title: world's shortest UI/UX design course

best.what: whole video: user flow -> wireframe -> design system -> design principles -> copy -> illustrations, one real project start to finish

why: Tight, correct, practical walk through the whole design process on one real project; names tools (Figma, Balsamiq) in passing but teaches the transferable steps, not tool mechanics.

title: Every UI/UX Concept Explained in Under 10 Minutes
why: nocaps, judged from title only. Same channel (Kole Jain) as HE4rLEQpiXY, which was strong and conceptual, so likely a decent rapid-fire glossary video, but unverified -- worth a quick human watch before slotting as core.

title: UI / UX Design Tutorial – Wireframe, Mockup & Design in Figma
why: nocaps, judged from title only: this is an 86-minute Figma software tutorial (freeCodeCamp). Kids won't use Figma -- Gemini builds the UI -- and wIuVvCuiJhU already covers the transferable concepts in 7 minutes.

title: This Video Will Take You From Junior to Senior UX/UI Designer

best.what: sleep-tracker app redesigned four times: personalization, visual hierarchy, emoji feedback, sliders -- a clean before/after case study
banking transfer screen redesign: reducing steps, recognition over recall, showing new balance -- another strong before/after case study

why: Repeated junior-vs-senior before/after redesigns make abstract principles (hierarchy, recognition over recall, progressive disclosure) concrete and are genuinely teen-followable; two ad breaks for the creator's own paid playbook/course should be skipped past.

title: How to think like a GENIUS UI/UX designer

best.what: whole video: design from user intent, respect layout conventions, structure content, animation with purpose, design systems as shared language

why: Dense but clear conceptual video (intent-first design, progressive disclosure, why design systems matter) with a real Airbnb-style example carried through; one short sponsor read (Mobin) is easy to skip.

title: How The Web Works - The Big Picture

best.what: whole video: domain -> DNS -> IP -> request/response -> HTML/CSS/JS -> HTTP/HTTPS -> server-side code -> apps and JSON -> websockets

why: The cleanest, most efficient explanation of client-server, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS and where JSON/APIs fit in the group -- exactly the mental model the course needs, in 12 minutes with no padding.

title: How a web application works
why: nocaps, judged from title only. On-topic and mid-length (35 min); likely overlaps heavily with hJHvdBlSxug so treat as a backup/alternate rather than adding both -- watch before deciding if it adds anything hJHvdBlSxug doesn't.

title: How does the internet work? (Full Course)

best.what: LAN/switch vs router basics, if a segment must be salvaged for a networking side-note

why: Sampled (102 min). This is a network-hardware course (switches, routers, ISPs, submarine cables, VPN tunneling, peering), not web/app development -- off-topic for kids building Sheets-backed web apps, extremely repetitive/padded, and hJHvdBlSxug already covers the actually-needed 'how does my app talk to a server' concept in 12 focused minutes.

title: APIs for Beginners - How to use an API (Full Course / Tutorial)

best.what: what an API/interface is, local vs remote APIs, why REST won, told through everyday analogies (remote controls, buttons, streaming apps) -- excellent standalone watch
closing 'RESTful scavenger hunt' review that recaps every REST constraint against the app they just built

why: Sampled (3h07m). The conceptual first ~18 minutes is the best explanation of APIs in the whole group and is fully teen-friendly on its own; the long middle build (Twilio account, curl, npm, VS Code, Vue) is well taught but needs an adult to set up accounts/installs first, so treat as a guided build-along, not a solo watch.

title: System Design Explained: APIs, Databases, Caching, CDNs, Load Balancing & Production Infra

best.what: single-server setup: domain -> DNS -> IP -> HTTP request/response, HTML for browsers vs JSON for apps
SQL vs NoSQL databases: tables/rows/joins/ACID vs document/key-value/graph stores, and when to use which -- directly useful for thinking about Sheets-as-database
HTTP status codes (200/201/400/401/404/500) and REST URL best practices (plural nouns, proper verbs)

why: Sampled (124 min). This is a senior-engineer / interview-prep system-design course -- load balancing, message queues, gRPC, OAuth2, CSRF/XSS defenses are well beyond a 14-15 y/o building an Apps Script game, but three early segments (client-server basics, SQL vs NoSQL, HTTP status codes) are clean, correct and directly relevant to the guide-writer, and could be clipped for kids with narration.

title: How the Web Works
why: 41-second fragment (looks like it was clipped from a longer Udacity course) that only restates 'browser and server talk over HTTP, server returns HTML' in one breath -- too thin to stand alone and fully redundant with hJHvdBlSxug's much fuller 12-minute version.
